name: MP1584 mini adjustable buck module
description: Tiny (23×17 mm) adjustable buck board, 4.5–28 V in to 0.8–20 V out, for wiring a cheap 5 V or 3.3 V supply into a hobby robot.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Sold as 3 A, but plan for about 1.5 A continuous (2 A peak) without extra cooling.
Single-turn trimmer: set and check the output before connecting the load.
EN is not broken out on most versions.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Input voltage 4.5-28 V. Two holes per connection.

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Output ground, connected to IN- on the module (non-isolated).

adjust.direction: clockwise lowers Vout; counter-clockwise raises Vout

notes: Four solder connections, each with two holes or pads. Labels are on the back. Seen from the back: OUT- and IN- along one long edge, OUT+ and IN+ along the other, with an arrow pointing from IN to OUT.
Hole spacing is 0.1 in side-to-side but not end-to-end, so the module does not plug directly into a breadboard.

Typical dropout is 1.6 V, and the output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.6 V (e.g. about 10.4 V from 12 V in). For best ripple, keep VIN at least 1.6-2 V above VOUT. The load condition for these figures is not stated.
The single-turn pot sets Vout to within a couple of percent (e.g. 4.95-5.05 V when aiming for 5 V).
Rated 1.5 A continuous and 2 A peak. The vendor does not recommend more than about 1.5 A long-term because of heat.
The IC has built-in over-current and thermal limiting. Reverse-polarity protection is not mentioned.
Uses ceramic capacitors, not electrolytics. Measured output ripple is 30-50 mV. Switching frequency is 1 MHz.
Wire the input and output before applying power, to avoid damaging the module. Components get hot under heavy load.
